decision: Substantial expansion of the existing McDonalds 1+1 guide; no duplicate page. Keep the app coupon and foodora campaigns distinct.

captures.method: Normal direct HTTPS GET with certificate validation; no authentication or access bypass

facts.app: The homepage still gives a 6-piece Chicken McNuggets 1+1 coupon as a MyMcDonalds example. Actual account availability and coupon terms were not inspected.

foodoraBreakfast.pairing: A second identical selected product accompanies purchase of the first.

facts.scope: Participating Austrian restaurants; while stocks last. Minimum order remains unchanged. No fixed product price or numerical minimum order is supplied in these terms.

captures.method: Normal direct HTTPS GET with certificate validation; ordinary public redirect followed
captures.finding: Public McDonalds ordering landing page is available. It did not independently display the breakfast campaign dates/products in the fetched HTML; merchant homepage is the source of those facts.

limits: No customer account or personal coupon read.
No address submitted and no order or redemption performed.
No particular Vienna restaurant, delivery availability, fees or basket behaviour verified.
No public universal coupon code, arbitrary product pairing, promotion stacking or free delivery promised.
30 November is the breakfast deadline, not the deadline for the 9 November foodora selection or the personal app coupon.
The guide keeps its original publication date 2026-10-30; dateModified is 2026-11-03. Its app content has no common expiry so data-deal-expires remains empty.
searchOpportunity: Foodora was an important search entry in the dated 2-29 October 2026 audit. No fresh Search Console values are asserted; Vienna breakfast planning and separating order channels are the new practical value.
